decision.title: Desktop splash owns its own recovery: the entry document navigates itself back via a no-input resolve_dev_server_url command
decision.rationale:
Issue #92 (dogfood): the app went black and sat on "Starting…" until force-quit. apps/desktop/src/index.html is the webview's ENTRY document and was pure static HTML with zero JavaScript; the only navigate-away-from-splash path is a ONE-SHOT in lib.rs setup(). So the app's usability rested on an unenforced invariant — 'the webview must never return to its entry document' — while WKWebView returns there on a content-process crash (WebKit reloads the window's ORIGINAL url) and on any uncaught back-navigation. Only one trigger (Backspace with shell focus) was guarded, in app.jsx, and not the dominant one.

DECISION: move part of the navigation responsibility from Rust into the entry document. The splash now carries an inline script that, on `pageshow`, invokes a NEW Tauri command `resolve_dev_server_url` and `location.replace()`s itself to the returned URL, retrying with backoff. This fixes EVERY return-to-entry trigger, named or not, instead of enumerating triggers one at a time.

SECURITY BOUNDARY (this is the load-bearing part, and it constrains any future edit): `resolve_dev_server_url` takes NO argument from the page. The project root comes from SidecarState (so a project switch is respected) and the URL from that project's own `_server.json`, run through server_json::is_loopback_url right there. The page receives an already-validated http://localhost:*/http://127.0.0.1:* string and can never steer the navigate. This keeps the DDR-109 §1 loopback-only invariant and the 'narrow command, trusted core' posture intact — the command must NOT grow a URL/path parameter, which would turn it into the open-navigate primitive DDR-054 forbids. It is granted to the remote dev-server origin in capabilities/default.json alongside the other narrow app commands.

`location.replace()` (not `.href`) is deliberate and has a second effect worth keeping: the splash overwrites its own history entry, so after first boot there is NO splash entry left for a back-navigation to land on. That closes the back-nav route into this bug at the source rather than intercepting keys, and is pinned by a test.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED AND DEFERRED (not rejected): (a) disabling WKWebView allowsBackForwardNavigationGestures + intercepting Cmd+[ / Cmd+left — needs objc2/objc2-app-kit promoted from transitive to DIRECT Cargo.toml deps, touching Cargo.lock, and it only covers the gesture trigger which self-recovery already covers; (b) a Rust-side on_page_load watchdog re-navigating on an unexpected return to the bundled-asset origin — belt-and-braces for the case where the page-side JS is itself wedged, but it must arm only AFTER the first successful startup navigate or it races the legitimate first-boot arrival at the splash. Both remain worthwhile hardening; neither is required for the reported bug.

COLD-START NUANCE: the command polls with a 5 s budget (RECOVERY_WAIT_MS), NOT the 120 s SERVER_WAIT_MS used at startup — a recovering splash asks about a server that is normally already up, and the page retries, so a miss is cheap. The page's 'still starting' notice waits 45 s so it does not cry wolf during a legitimate first-run boot-self-heal (bun install + build), which can take ~90 s.

EVIDENCE: reproduced red then verified green through a new desktop E2E scenario, apps/desktop/e2e/scenarios/splash-recovers-after-return-to-entry.e2e.ts, which simulates the crash-reload by navigating the webview straight at tauri://localhost. Note for future editors: `history.back()` can NO LONGER reach the splash once the fix is in (that is the replace() property above), so the crash-reload simulation — not a history navigation — is the correct way to reproduce this state. Plus 5 Rust unit tests on the loopback validation in server_json.rs.
